Coming here from #40719 (which I closed as a duplicate of this one). Adding the technical detail in case it helps a future implementation.

I have a working local impl I'd be glad to PR against this issue. The approach mirrors the existing `@` mention trigger:

- Extract a shared `tokenTriggerIndex(value, offset, trigger)` helper from `mentionTriggerIndex` in `packages/tui/src/prompt/display.ts` so `/` and `@` share one code path instead of parallel logic.
- Add `slashTriggerIndex` reusing the same whitespace-preceded rule, so `foo /comp` triggers but `https://x`, `foo/bar`, `MM/DD` do not. Newline counts as a separator; Unicode display width goes through the existing `promptOffsetWidth` path.
- Make `server-command` `onSelect` and `hide()` in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx` index-aware, so selecting a command mid-line replaces only the typed token, not the whole line.
- Reopen the menu when the cursor steps back onto a `/` token anywhere in the line, mirroring the `@` reopen path. Start-of-line case (`store.index === 0`) is preserved unchanged.

One edge worth flagging: `/` shows up in prose far more often than `@` (paths, URLs, dates, division). The whitespace-preceded rule rejects `https://` and `foo/bar`, but reviewers may want extra guards for things that look like dates or URL fragments.

Tests: added a `slashTriggerIndex` suite in `packages/tui/test/prompt/display.test.ts` mirroring the mention-trigger cases. All green.

Happy to open the PR once there's sign-off on the direction.
Closing as a duplicate of #40689 (filed a couple of hours earlier, same request). Moved the technical detail and implementation sketch over there so it's not lost.

Coming here from #40720 (closed as a duplicate of this one). This issue captures the core ask (skills invocable as `/name` at root), but a few UX decisions fall out of it that any implementation will need to settle. Dropping them here so they're part of the design conversation:

1. **Curation vs discoverability.** Once skills show at root, users with many skills installed see a longer list. Default-on, opt-in (e.g., a setting like `tui.skillsAtRoot`), or scoped (show skills at root only when the typed query after `/` matches one)?

2. **Ordering.** Should skills sort after built-ins (current `/skills` grouping preserved visually), interleave by frecency, or keep the existing `slashes()` first then everything else?

3. **Labeling.** Today MCP commands get a `:mcp` suffix in the description. Should skills get an analogous marker (e.g., `(skill)`) so users can tell what they are invoking at a glance?

The current root autocomplete skips them explicitly (`if (serverCommand.source === "skill") continue` in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx`), so flipping that one line is the code change. The hard part is the design call above.

Note also: this depends on the mid-line `/` plumbing being index-aware so picking a long skill name mid-line replaces only the typed token. That work is being tracked in #40689.

Closing as a duplicate of #35341 (filed a month earlier, same outcome: skills invocable from the root `/` list). Moved the three design questions (curation vs discoverability, ordering, labeling) over there since any implementation will need to answer them.

Adding field measurements and a scope note, since this has been sitting a while and I've since learned the fix here is narrower than the bug.

**Measured exposure.** On one long-running box (`build` agent pinned to `anthropic/claude-opus-5` in config), from the local session store:

- **75 of 89** `build` sessions (84.3%) have a session-row model that differs from the agent's configured model.
- **59,289 of 69,382** `build`-agent assistant turns (85.5%) ran on something other than the configured model.

So for a config that pins an agent model, the resolution order `input.model ?? ag.model ?? currentModel(...)` picks the wrong model roughly six times out of seven whenever an injected prompt omits `model`. `currentModel()` itself is fine — it reads the session row — it just never gets consulted, because `ag.model` preempts it. That ordering is the whole bug, and it only bites when an agent config sets a model (which is why it's easy to miss in a default setup).

**Scope note against this PR.** What I did here fixes the *caller*: `task.ts` now resolves the model itself and passes it explicitly. That closes #38770's reported path, but it leaves the resolution order untouched, so any other injector that omits `model` still lands on `ag.model`. In current `dev` that includes `session/compaction.ts`, and it will include any future injector, since omitting `model` looks like the natural thing to do.

I've since been running a resolver-side variant instead, which changes `createUserMessage` to prefer the durable session row ahead of `ag.model`:

```ts
const switched = !!current.agent && ag.name !== current.agent
const sessionModel = !switched && current.model ? { /* from session row */ } : undefined
const model = input.model ?? sessionModel ?? prev?.info.model ?? ag.model ?? (yield* currentModel(input.sessionID))
```

The `switched` guard is the load-bearing part: a genuine agent switch must still adopt the new agent's configured model, while an injected prompt for the *current* agent keeps the session model. It also carries the variant through, which is the same thing this PR's `prompt.ts` hunk is reaching for.

That approach covers every injector at once rather than one call site at a time. I'm not pushing it into this PR unprompted — it's a broader change and the ordering question is really a maintainer call. Happy to do either:

1. keep this PR as the narrow #38770 fix, and open a separate one for the resolution order; or
2. replace this PR's contents with the resolver fix and let it close the class.

Say which you'd prefer and I'll turn it around. I have the resolver version already running with tests, though they're written against a diverged local tree, so I'd rewrite them against `dev`'s harness before submitting.

One caveat on my numbers, stated plainly: they come from a single heavily-used installation, so treat them as an existence proof for the exposure rather than a population estimate. Anyone whose agents don't pin a model won't see this at all.

The error you're seeing ("ResourceExhausted: Worker local total request limit reached") indicates the upstream NVIDIA NIM worker has hit its concurrency limit — this is a known capacity issue with the free tier model.

Came here from the same gap — I independently arrived at the same core (`todo.updated` → `sessionUpdate: "plan"`), which makes me confident the approach is right. +1 to ship this.

On the open thread: I'd drop the `session.idle` cleanup. The ACP plan spec only describes the agent reporting status, not finalizing it at turn end. @axel7083's concern is real — a turn that ends to ask the user something would mark every started item completed, which is misleading. The `todo.updated` mapping + fingerprint dedup already give correct live progress; the cleanup adds risk for no spec benefit.

If you're low on bandwidth I'm happy to open a PR against this branch that removes the idle cleanup and rebases onto current `dev`, so this can move. Just say the word.

Closing as a duplicate of #31834 — it implements the same `todo.updated → plan` mapping and is further along (fingerprint dedup, richer tests). I'll help move #31834 forward instead of fragmenting the effort.

I don't think this is a duplicate.

* **#32432** specifically describes **cancelled** subagents that cannot be opened.
* **#34457** mentions **incomplete** task calls, but my issue consistently affects **all running subagents**, even during normal execution without any cancellation.

In my case, as long as a subagent is still running, clicking its task entry does nothing. The only way to inspect it is to first open another subagent (typically a completed one) and then use the previous/next navigation to switch to the running subagent.

Additionally, **Ctrl+X is consistently non-functional whenever there is at least one running subagent**. The shortcut only starts working again after all subagents have finished.

So this appears to affect the interaction with **active** subagents in general, not just cancelled ones.

Additional isolation data:
On the same machine (macOS 26.6 arm64, Bun 1.3.14), running the exact web-tree-sitter flow that packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts uses — Parser.init() → Language.load(tree-sitter-bash.wasm) → parse("echo hello") — with the system-installed Bun 1.3.14 succeeds:

parse OK: (program (command name: (command_name (word)) argument: (word)))

WebAssembly.compile() of web-tree-sitter@0.25.10's wasm also succeeds with system bun. So the WASM asset and Bun 1.3.14 work fine outside opencode. Only opencode's compiled binary (brew, 1.18.13 & 1.18.14 both) fails with H.loadWebAssemblyModule, every time, TUI and headless. Narrowing it to a build/embedding issue in the release binary (embedded WASM asset or JSC wasm binding) on macOS arm64.

Thank you to the maintainers for all the hard work — OpenCode's core is genuinely great, and we appreciate the constant shipping.

But I have to be blunt about the v2 desktop layout: the new design is significantly harder to use than what it replaced. The sidebar gave you one-glance access to all projects, workspaces, and sessions — and you could pin/favorite conversations so long-running projects stayed visible at all times. The new tab-based layout buries all of that behind multiple clicks, makes switching between projects/worktrees painful, and wastes huge amounts of screen space on large monitors. Worse, even basic session management is missing: there is no pin or favorite for conversations at all. A session tool that drops its most-used organizational feature — you had a reference implementation right in front of you, the old layout itself — and even that wasn't copied properly. I'd honestly expect better.

Please at least restore the old layout toggle for new installs (currently gated behind `oldLayoutEligible`, which fresh installs never get), or bring the sidebar back as a first-class option — with pin/favorite support. Forcing everyone onto a layout a large part of the community is loudly rejecting is how you lose users.

And one last thing: a sudden flash of bad ideas is far scarier than making no effort at all. When you act on impulse and get it wrong, at least the people who never tried have an excuse — you don't.


The client passes back **standard Anthropic-format thinking blocks** in `messages` (e.g. `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"...","signature":"..."}`), yet the Zen **Console** gateway still returns this 400.

Observed on 2026-08-04 from a Claude Code desktop client (cc-haha v0.5.3) proxying Anthropic-format requests to `https://opencode.ai/zen`. Notes:

- Plain-text and tool-call turns with the same thinking-block pass-back **succeed**.
- The failure appears specific to turns involving **image / multimodal content combined with thinking pass-back** (27 of 28 errors in the session were on image requests).
- Error source is `provider (Console)`, not the direct DeepSeek or `go` gateway.
